articles.headline: Sean Payton's replay challenge results in key interception in Broncos' victory
articles.description: Denver coach Sean Payton's replay challenge with 1 minute, 30 seconds left in the third quarter, turned an incomplete pass in the endzone into an improbable interception by Broncos safety Devon Key during his club's 26-21 win at Bank of America Stadium.
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- In the end, a red challenge flag, wrapped with three rubber bands around two ounces of sand and thrown by Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton late in the third quarter Sunday, left the Carolina Panthers heated and the Broncos flush with a 26-21 win at Bank of America Stadium.

Payton's replay challenge, with 1 minute, 30 seconds left in the third quarter, turned an incomplete pass in the Broncos' endzone into an improbable interception by Broncos reserve safety Devon Key. The Panthers led 14-13 at the time and the Broncos out-scored the Panthers, 13-8, the rest of the way for their now NFL record 16th consecutive win in a one-score game.

"We never flinch when those situations are upon us," Key said. " ... I wouldn't say it's luck ... it takes everyone in the building to do what we do."

It all started as a first-and-goal play from the Broncos' 1-yard line. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young tried to squeeze a pass in to tight end Tommy Tremble near the back left corner of the endzone. Broncos' linebacker Justin Strnad collided with Tremble as the ball arrived.

As Tremble and Strnad fell to the ground, replays showed the ball bounced off of Tremble's right forearm and Key then snatched just inches from the ground. The played was initially ruled an incomplete pass and the Panthers rushed to the line of  scrimmage to  then ran a play as running back Chuba Hubbard was stopped for no gain.

But referee Alan Eck announced after the Hubbard run Payton had thrown the challenge flag before the Panthers had snapped the ball on the  play.

"I didn't know after we ran another play that they could go back for it," Tremble said. "That was confusing to us, to a lot of us on offense, but in football, stuff like that happens. What can you do about it?"

In a pool report with Eck and the NFL's vice president of instant replay Alan Butterworth, Eck said Key's interception was reviewed to make sure he caught the ball before it hit the ground and the NFL's replay center had also determined Payton had thrown the challenge flag before the Panthers had snapped the ball on the next play.

"Replay can get involved to make sure that the head coach throws his challenge flag prior to the next snap," Butterworth said. "We were actually able to use angles to show that the flag was out prior to the ball being snapped, and so we permitted the challenge."

Payton said the Broncos' Director of Game Management Evan Rothstein, who is also an assistant quarterbacks coach, is the voice in his ear -- "it's Evan, it's not a group vote" -- on decisions to challenge a play. He said Rothstein told him, shouted actually, for Payton to throw the challenge flag just before the Panthers had snapped the ball on the next play.

"I just gave Evan a game ball," Payton said. "That was a hard one for any of us to see and my concern was were they able, was anyone able, to see I threw it before the play was snapped. Fortunately, New York can ...  that one, that's the first I can ever r

articles.headline: NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 9.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Madrid with the Bengals' offense erupting in a win over the Falcons. Cincinnati wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with a season-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions.

Back in the United States, Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returned from injury, finishing with three sacks in a win over the Commanders. Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders fell to the Saints in his first start of the 2026 season. And quarterback Bo Nix led the Broncos to their fifth fourth-quarter comeback this year -- tied for the most through nine games in NFL history, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game -- including how teams will approach Tuesday's trade deadline. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

DAL-IND | CLE-NO | NYG-PHI

NYJ-KC | DEN-CAR | LAR-WSH

DET-MIA | CIN-ATL

Catch up on Thursday's game:

JAX-BAL

Dallas 27, Indianapolis 23

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys

Should the Cowboys make a trade at the deadline? At 4-5, the Cowboys have one fewer win than the NFC East-leading Giants (5-2-1), so they are still in the division race ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. As tempting as it might be, owner and general manager Jerry Jones said on the 105.3 The Fan pregame show Sunday, "At this point, I don't see it." The Cowboys made their big trade already for CB Joey Porter Jr. and don't have a ton of assets to make a substantive move. Would it really make a difference? If they want to replicate 2018, when they started 3-5 and made the playoffs after trading for WR Amari Cooper, it will likely be with the current roster.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys' defense looked competent in the first half for the second straight game. Against Arizona, they allowed 129 yards and no TDs. Against the Colts, they allowed a touchdown but only 79 yards -- the fewest by Dallas in a first half since Week 18 of 2024 against the Commanders. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Colts

Will Sunday's loss impact trade deadline decisions? The Colts have been heavily involved in trade discussions since GM Chris Ballard was fired last month; they've already traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. But the word around the team Sunday was that the Colts were less likely to make a splashy deal than to do one. Still, falling to 2-7 and suffering a fifth straight loss could impact principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon's thinking. Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are among the most discussed trade possibilities, and quarterback Daniel Jones is a more remote possibility.

articles.headline: John Harbaugh: Giants did pull offer for Jonathan Taylor but 'things do change'
articles.description: The Giants pulled a recent trade offer for Jonathan Taylor, according to coach John Harbaugh, who added that doesn't mean a deal is completely off the table.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Giants pulled a recent trade offer for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, according to coach John Harbaugh, who added that doesn't mean a deal is completely off the table.

Fox Sports reported Sunday morning that the Giants offered the Colts a second- and a fifth-round pick for Taylor.

Harbaugh was asked about that offer after the Giants' win over the Eagles later Sunday.

"I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place," he said following the 19-11 victory. "If something happens for any player, can't talk about any [specific] player because they're with other teams right now, but we're not ruling anything out."

ESPN's Adam Schefter has reported the Giants and Colts didn't have much contact this past week. The Colts, in sell mode amid a 2-7 season, have maintained a high price for Taylor, sources said. 

The Giants (5-2-1) are interested in improving their team. The question is at what cost. They're in the driver's seat in the NFC East, and running back is a position where an upgrade is viable if Taylor is available.

Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missed Sunday's game and Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) is on injured reserve. Devin Singletary was the team's lead back against the Eagles and had 31 yards on 21 carries.

An NFL source said this past week he could still see the Giants adding an interior defensive lineman, also a position of need, before a running back.

"I don't see anything particularly imminent right now either," Harbaugh said. "So we'll see what happens."

Harbaugh already said earlier in the week he made a personal call to Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about the availability of defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons. The Giants were also interested in Commanders defensive lineman Daron Payne before he was lost for the season with a foot injury.

No door is shut. Not on Taylor or anybody else.

"I will say this, things do change," Harbaugh said about the Taylor trade being dead. "Things change from day to day."

Any move has to make sense for the present and future. New York already lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and top pass rusher Brian Burns for the season with injuries. It's on a third starting quarterback with J.J. McCarthy, who left and later returned to Sunday's contest with a hip injury.

"I'm not just gonna go for a short-term fix at exorbitant cost. That's not where we're at," Harbaugh said. "And usually when you do that sort of thing, it doesn't work out for you. You end paying a hefty price and don't get the return on it. I never think that you're one step way or one player away, to me it's always just a total momentum kind of thing anyway.

"But if the right opportunity comes and there's a deal that makes sense for us, we'll do it."

articles.headline: Barça pass their biggest test yet as Fermín López sinks Atlético Madrid
articles.description: Needing a response after losing to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, Barcelona came from behind at Atlético on Sunday to underline their title credentials.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Fermín López produced two finishes of the highest quality as Barcelona came from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2-1 on Sunday at the Metropolitano to claim their biggest win of the season so far.

It was a victory which was much needed after back-to-back defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in October. Barça had scored 60 goals in 15 games -- an average of four per match -- heading into this weekend's trip to Atlético, but those losses had raised question marks about whether they could step up against better opposition when it really matters.

Those questions may return at some point -- Atlético were the better side in the first half -- but Hansi Flick's side's reaction to those setbacks has been good. After hammering Alavés in LaLiga and beating Aston Villa in the UEFA Champions League, victory against Diego Simeone's side ensured they remain the top of the league. With 11 wins from 12 games, they have a three-point cushion over Real Madrid, while Atlético are now five points back.

- Anthony Gordon left Premier League to get 'respect' -- he's got it now

- Man Utd's poor starts have Premier League relegation looking more likely

- Liverpool's Barcola, Isak, Wirtz show signs they're finally starting to click

The build-up to Sunday's game was dripping with narrative. Last season's meetings between the two teams were still very much present. Barça beat Atlético twice in LaLiga en route to back-to-back titles only to suffer painful eliminations to the Rojiblancos in the Copa del Rey and, especially, the Champions League.

However, the main focus was on Julián Álvarez. This was the first time the two teams had met since the Atleti striker tried to engineer a summer transfer to Barça. He missed several chances here, although he did set up the early opener for Giuliano Simeone.

Before the game, the home fans unveiled a giant tifo with the words "Mi dulce condena" -- "My sweet sentence" -- alongside an anonymous Atlético player behind bars. It felt like a nod to Álvarez being reluctantly forced to stay at the club after saying it would "be best for everyone" if a transfer could be agreed.

In a fast-paced start to the game, the Argentina international had a great early chance to make amends by opening the scoring. One-on-one with Joan García, he attempted to round the Barça goalkeeper, but was forced too wide and the chance was gone. Marc Pubill thumped the bar from the resulting corner; Pedri then hit the woodwork at the other end. This was all within seven minutes.

Three minutes later, Atlético led. A simple switch of play caused Barça's defence all sorts of problems, Álvarez squared and Simeone, who had lost João Cancelo, turned home.

Álvarez, after another Cancelo mistake, then saw another effort stopped by García, the ball snaking towards the line after the save but cleared by Barça eventually.

Barça grew into the game before the break, but there was still an element of surprise about their equaliser just before half-time.

articles.headline: Nuggets' starters all questionable vs. Rockets after delays leaving Mexico
articles.description: Hampered by plane delays leaving Mexico City, the Nuggets have listed their entire starting lineup as questionable for Monday's game in Houston.
articles.body:
The Denver Nuggets have had major plane delays exiting Mexico City and are listing all of their starters as questionable for Monday night's game in Houston.

The Nuggets beat the Indiana Pacers 114-102 on Saturday afternoon in a neutral-site international game in Mexico City and were scheduled to leave Saturday night, but issues with their aircraft forced them back to the hotel early Sunday morning.

They were scheduled and hopeful they would take off for Houston on Sunday night for a Monday night game against the Rockets. But in response to the travel problems, the team canceled Monday's shootaround and listed Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray, Aaron Gordon, Cameron Johnson, DeMar DeRozan and Christian Braun with various ailments.

The Nuggets are 5-3. The Rockets are 7-3.

articles.headline: Saints reference Shedeur Sanders quote after win, leading NFL Week 9 trolls
articles.description: The New Orleans Saints kept the receipts and poked fun at Shedeur Sanders to lead NFL Week 9 trolls.
articles.body:
The United States' Miranda Warning states: "Anything you say can and will be used against you in a court of law." That same sentiment was exercised by the New Orleans Saints in their social media caption after their Week 9 victory.

New Orleans held on to defeat the Cleveland Browns 23-22 in overtime to get back in the win column. Cleveland attempted a two-point conversion after a touchdown late in the extra period, but New Orleans forced a stop for the victory.

Quarterback Shedeur Sanders started for the Browns with Deshaun Watson inactive after suffering a concussion. Sanders, making his first start of the season, was asked Wednesday about what he's seen from the Saints' defense. He flashed a grin before saying: "I've seen a lot. When I smile just know that means something."

New Orleans remembered the comment, captioning its post with the quote and using an image of players doing Sanders' signature celebration.

Here are the top NFL trolls from Week 9.

Los Angeles Rams 20, Washington Commanders 13

The Los Angeles Rams are winners of three straight after beating the Washington Commanders.

Playing alongside Aaron Donald for the first time, Myles Garrett put up three sacks and a forced fumble as the Rams' defense flexed its muscles. On the offensive side, wide receiver Puka Nacua caught 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown.

Los Angeles went deep in the archives to poke fun at Washington. The Rams referenced a 1976 segment of "Schoolhouse Rock!" an educational series, titled "I'm Just A Bill." The musical chronicles how a bill passes through the Capitol Building in Washington D.C. to become a law. Often shown in social studies classes, the main character is a rolled up piece of paper with "bill" on the front.

Los Angeles put its own spin on the famous episode, putting "Rams" on the bill and a "W" behind it in a font similar to "Schoolhouse Rock!" The caption? "It's just a dub!"

New York Giants 19, Philadelphia Eagles 11

The New York Giants gutted out a win against the Philadelphia Eagles on the road -- New York's first road win against Philadelphia since 2013, according to ESPN Research.

The low-scoring affair included 463 combined total yards and just two touchdowns. The Giants defense recorded seven sacks -- their most in a game since Week 13 in 2024 -- with rookie linebacker Arvell Reese having three of them.

Playing in the city known for cheesesteaks, New York poked fun at Philadelphia by ripping a cheesesteak in half and placing it on a plate with the game's score above it. The Giants shared a fast-paced video packed with jabs at Philadelphia, including a variety of bald eagle memes and a clip of LeBron James.

Cincinnati Bengals 34, Atlanta Falcons 17

Trolls sometimes go international, too. The Cincinnati Bengals took down the Atlanta Falcons in the NFL's annual game in Madrid.

articles.headline: Myles Garrett has three sacks in return to help Rams stop Commanders
articles.description: Myles Garrett had three sacks in his return to the field for the Rams in Los Angeles' victory over the Commanders.
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- As Myles Garrett sat at the podium after the Los Angeles Rams' Week 1 loss and acknowledged he was playing through a knee injury, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year said his performance in the game was "the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

But in his first game back from his mid-September knee surgery, Garrett was a difference-maker for the Rams. In Los Angeles' 20-13 victory against the Washington Commanders, Garrett had six pressures and three sacks on 27 pass rushes (22.2% pressure rate), according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He played 35 of 58 defensive snaps (60.3%).

While Garrett said he was "nowhere near" to the performance he knows he is capable of, it felt "great to be out there with my teammates again."

"Man, it was a weight off my shoulders, just getting back to who I am," Garrett said. "I'm nowhere near where I want to be as far as my performance and things I know I can do and how I can move, but this is a confidence booster for sure."

The game marked the first time that Garrett and defensive tackle Aaron Donald played together. According to NFL NGS, with both players on the field (23 plays), the Rams' defense allowed 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. On all other plays (19), the defense allowed 8.0 yards per play and a touchdown with no sacks.

"We got a pretty good feel of the game, was able to play off each other sometime and do some things, so it was fun," Donald said.

Garrett's first sack of the game was a strip sack of Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in the second quarter.

"I tried to step up and I'd seen I want to say Van [Jefferson] on a corner route and I was trying to throw it and then Myles Garrett happened," Daniels said.

Since Donald initially retired in March 2024, the Rams have been looking for their closer on defense. Rams coach Sean McVay said Sunday that Garrett "did a great job being able to close the game out and make his presence felt."

When asked whether he felt he could fill that role for the Rams, Garrett said, "I am that closer. So we don't need to look any further."

Two of Garrett's three sacks came in the fourth quarter. One of those sacks came up the middle against rookie center Matt Gulbin, subbing for an injured Lucas Patrick.

"It's a hard ask to go out there and go one on one vs. Myles Garrett when they put him up there," Commanders guard Sam Cosmi said.

The game was Garrett's ninth career three-sack game, the most by any player since Hall-of-Famer DeMarcus Ware in 2014, according to ESPN Research.

Garrett now has 128.5 sacks in his NFL career, which tied Hall of Famer Jared Allen for the second-most by any player within his first 10 seasons since sacks became official in 1982.

ESPN's John Keim contributed to this story.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Should Man United's equalizing goal have been allowed?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

Photo credit: USA Sports, NBC

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Did Lammens interfere with Suzuki?

Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa (Nov. 8)

Referee: Chris Kavanagh

VAR: Craig Pawson

Time: 96 minutes

Incident: Possible foul in Manchester United's equalizing goal.

What happened: Bruno Fernandes swung in a last-chance corner kick as Man United threw every player they had on the pitch, including keeper Senne Lammens, into the penalty area.

Patrick Dorgu outjumped the Aston Villa defenders and, with keeper Zion Suzuki flapping at the ball, nodded home what seemed like a straightforward header into the net. However, Suzuki believed he was fouled by opposite number Lammens as the United No. 1 attempted to block the Villa keeper -- Lammens made contact with Suzuki while neither looking at the ball nor making any attempt to play it.

Referee Kavanagh was unmoved by the appeals, yellow-carding Suzuki for his protests and awarding the goal.

VAR decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision of goal.

VAR review: VAR checked the incident and was comfortable that although Lammens clearly had intent to disturb Suzuki from having a clear path to punch the ball away by bumping into him, any contact was minimal and, more importantly, his impact on the Villa keeper was a 50-50 call. This is a ratio where VAR is not keen to get involved and will stick with the on-field decision.

Verdict: VAR were correct not to intervene in this situation as it fell short of the threshold for a clear on-field error.

Though Lammens' intention was obvious, intent is not a punishable offense, and the many replays didn't evidence enough of an impactful physical action on Suzuki that met the criteria for an intervention. However, Lammens did gamble with this play, and if referee Kavanagh had judged his action differently and awarded a late free kick to Villa, United could have few complaints.

This was a borderline call either way, and I am comfortable that the on-field decision should stick regardless of which way it fell.

Arsenal robbed of a penalty

Arsenal 1-0 Hull City (Nov. 7)

Referee: Farai Hallam

VAR: Michael Oliver

Time: 42 minutes

Incident: Penalty not awarded to Arsenal for an offside offense.

articles.headline: Jalen Duren to miss at least two more weeks with hamstring injury
articles.description: Jalen Duren will miss at least two more weeks because of a hamstring injury, the Detroit Pistons announced Sunday.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Jalen Duren will miss at least two more weeks because of a hamstring injury, the Detroit Pistons announced Sunday.

The 22-year-old All-Star center was injured in Detroit's second game of the season, a 128-111 win over the Miami Heat on Oct. 23. He has missed six games and is expected to miss at least six more. The team said Duren has been cleared for full basketball participation.

Duren, who signed a five-year, $200 million contract extension before the season, averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds last season, but fell off to 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds in 14 playoff games.

articles.headline: Brown, Maxey and James combine for 78 points in 76ers' 127-121 win over Bulls
articles.description: — Jaylen Brown scored 29 points, Tyrese Maxey added 27 and LeBron James had his highest-scoring effort so far in a Philadelphia uniform as the 76ers held off the struggling Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Jaylen Brown scored 29 points, Tyrese Maxey added 27 and LeBron James had his highest-scoring effort so far in a Philadelphia uniform as the 76ers held off the struggling Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday afternoon.


              James had a season-high 22 for the 76ers, who got 18 points and 10 rebounds from Joel Embiid and 13 points from VJ Edgecombe.


              At 9-2, the 76ers — the Eastern Conference leaders — are off to their best 11-game start since going 10-1 to open the 2000-01 season.


              Josh Giddey had 19 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds for Chicago. Matas Buzelis added 19 points for the Bulls, who got 18 from Caleb Wilson, 17 from Jalen Smith, 12 from Isaac Okoro and 10 from Noa Essengue.


              The Bulls dropped their seventh straight and fell to 1-8, tying the third-worst nine-game start in team history. Chicago started 0-9 was in 1967-68 — the franchise’s second season — and 2004-05.


              James' 3-pointer 3:15 into the game gave him 1,897 career points against Chicago, making him the all-time leading scorer against the Bulls. Abdul-Jabbar — who was the NBA's all-time leading scorer, until James passed him for the No. 1 spot in 2023 — scored 1,895 points against the Bulls in 76 games; James was playing a regular season game against Chicago for the 70th time.


              Brown made 11 of 22 shots from the floor in his final game before facing his former team — the Boston Celtics — in a real game for the first time. The teams met in the preseason, making the first time Brown went up against the team that traded him to Philadelphia this past offseason, but Tuesday's game in Philadelphia will be the first time Brown faces the Celtics in a game that counts in the standings.


              Up next
              76ers: Host Boston on Tuesday.


              Bulls: Host San Antonio on Wednesday.


              ------
